meeting_header:
Date: 2025-02-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Liu (Redwood SE), Andre Gomez (Redwood CSM), Tom Bennett (MiraQ CTO), Rina Shah (MiraQ Lead ML), Daniel Lee (MiraQ SRE), Hannah Park (MiraQ Product), Liam O'Connor (MiraQ Procurement)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Uh, quick roll call — I see Tom, Rina, Daniel. Can you all hear me?
[00:08] Tom - MiraQ: Yeah, loud and clear. Thanks Jordan.
[00:12] Jordan (AE): Awesome. Agenda for today: quick recap of last week's model runs, dig into the version gateway idea Maya's been prototyping, decide on pin/window strategy for the pilot, and list next steps.
[00:25] Maya (SE): Quick note — the gateway work is on the branch I mentioned in Slack, it's a light routing layer that can pin traffic to a model version but also do a soft fallback when the pinned variant misses SLOs. I prototyped two flavors: immediate hard pin vs gateway with rolling weights.
[00:40] Rina - MiraQ: When you say "soft fallback" do you mean we let some percent go to the backup model, or is it a shadow pass?
[00:46] Maya (SE): Good question. It's configurable: you can do canary-style shadowing — no user response — or weighted routing where X% of live traffic goes to fallback. For our pilot I suggested a 95/5 soft lane for a couple hours to surface quality deltas without blasting latency.
[01:05] Daniel - MiraQ (SRE): How do we measure the tradeoff? p95 vs delta-accuracy? Our SLA is 200ms p95 for the agent flows.
[01:13] Maya (SE): We capture p50/p95/p99 in the console and also token-level time deltas. The prototype stores both latency and a simple quality score from our eval harness — F1-ish on our labeled prompts. There's a dashboard linked in the pilot doc.
[01:30] Hannah - MiraQ: I noticed that in the spreadsheet the smaller quantized model had lower cost but worse hallucination rate on the retrieval prompts — is that what you saw too?
[01:38] Maya (SE): Yeah, exactly. The q4_1 run reduced per-token GPU time but the hallucination metric jumped ~6 points on that subset. So the idea is: pin the high-quality variant for critical flows, route background/less-sensitive flows to cheaper variants, and keep a soft fallback lane so we can roll back gradually.
[01:55] Tom - MiraQ: On rollbacks — are we doing full rollbacks, or is there a rollforward that increments weight back to the safe model? I heard you mention rollforward in the doc but want to understand ops impact.
[02:05] Maya (SE): We support both. Rollback is immediate: revert routing to a previous fixed version. Rollforward is weight-based — e.g., move from 80/20 to 100/0 in steps. Rollforward is safer for noisy signals. For urgent incidents you can trigger a hard fallback route that pins everything to the previous version.
[02:24] Daniel - MiraQ: And that hard fallback triggers an event in the Redwood console and an alert webhook?
[02:29] Andre (Redwood CSM): Yep, Maya's prototype raises an incident flag and we can wire your PagerDuty. We also send a structured trace showing which requests tripped the threshold — though, fair warning, sometimes the transcription of model name in our logs looks like "R E D wood" if autosub mis-parses, so you'll want to map IDs.
[02:45] Liam - MiraQ: Security question — any change to data residency when we flip routing between hosted and dedicated models? We need to keep EU data in EU region for GDPR.
[02:53] Jordan (AE): Good call. The gateway respects region constraints; you can define routing policies by region. For the pilot we can pin EU traffic to the EU-dedicated pool. Also KMS/HSM keys remain in customer-controlled VPC for Private deployments.
[03:10] Rina - MiraQ: One of our engineers asked about KV cache — is prefix caching preserved across a model variant switch? If we soft-fallback some traffic, do we lose KV context and blow up latency?
[03:21] Maya (SE): The runtime keeps KV cache per-session key rather than per-version where the model architecture and tokenizer are compatible. So if the variant is the same architecture and tokenization, caches can be reused. If you switch across different tokenizers there's a warmup penalty. I'll add a note in the playbook about cache affinity.
[03:40] Tom - MiraQ: That warmup could impact our p95 in the first hour after a pin. Can we pre-warm?
[03:45] Maya (SE): Yes — pre-warm scripts are supported. We can replay a small set of representative prompts to refill KV. The gate can optionally trigger a pre-warm before flipping weights to 100/0.
[03:54] Jordan (AE): Quick housekeeping — we got your security checklist, Liam, and Maya will attach the updated rollback YAML.
[04:00] [00:04:00] Jordan (AE): Ok let's jump into the run results — Rina you ran the curated prompts collection against the candidate set?
[04:08] Rina - MiraQ: Yep. Results summary: Model A (base open model v1.3) — p95 180ms, quality score 0.84; Model B (quantized q4_1) — p95 140ms, quality 0.78 with hallucination bump on retrieval prompts; Model C (redwood-optimized v2) — p95 190ms, quality 0.87.
[04:28] Maya (SE): Interesting that redwood-optimized is a bit slower p95 but better quality. That matches expectation for more compute-heavy kernels. For flows where quality is critical, Model C looks best.
[04:40] Tom - MiraQ: Are those numbers with batching on? Our real traffic has microbursts; we care about both single-request latency and small batch behavior.
[04:47] Maya (SE): The spreadsheet shows both single and batch figures. Single-request p95 is as above; with batching (batch size 4) the cost per-token drops and p95 for Model C moves to ~160ms in our env. I'll push the per-route CSV.
[05:00] [00:05:00] Daniel - MiraQ: On the subject of model IDs: can we pin by semantic tag (e.g., prod-2025-02-01) or do we need to pin by hash? We want to keep releases readable.
[05:08] Maya (SE): You can pin by either. For safety we recommend pinning by immutable hash in the rollout but keep a semantic alias that you can swap. The gateway supports both alias-to-hash mapping so the UI shows friendly names.
[05:20] Hannah - MiraQ: Procurement here — if we go into dedicated pools during the pilot how much extra does that add? We need a rough delta to decide.
[05:27] Jordan (AE): I can send a delta estimate. Short answer: dedicated reserved slices are more predictable and remove noisy noisy multi-tenant spikes; cost will be higher than burst-hosted but you get SLA. I'll follow up with a 3-line pricing compare.
[05:38] [00:06:00] Tom - MiraQ: Back to fallback logic — suppose Model C degrades in quality by X% over baseline — what's the automatic threshold you suggest to trigger a soft fallback vs hard rollback?
[05:48] Maya (SE): Default we see teams use a 3–5% drop in quality score or collision of latency SLO breach for two consecutive 5-minute windows to trigger an automated soft fallback. Hard rollback tends to be manual or a >10% quality regression. We can tune those thresholds per route.
[06:05] Rina - MiraQ: Does Redwood capture downstream error types (e.g., malformed outputs, safety filter hits) as part of the quality signal?
[06:11] Maya (SE): Yes we can add safety hits, parsing errors, and custom QA metrics into the regression signal. You can weight them. Many teams weight hallucination higher for retrieval tasks.
[06:24] [00:07:00] Liam - MiraQ: From a procurement/legal angle — if we keep a warm shadow on a hosted fallback, are we double-billing tokens? How does billing work when we shadow?
[06:33] Jordan (AE): Shadowing is billed for compute used by the shadow pass. We can offer a pilot credit against shadowed tokens. We'll call that out in the pilot MOU.
[06:43] Tom (MiraQ): One item we should decide today — final model subset for locked pilot. Rina, what's your recommendation?
[06:48] Rina - MiraQ: I'd lock Model C for critical flows, Model B for bulk background, and Model A as a mid-cost fallback. Use gateway to route. Proposal: 70% Model C on critical, 30% Model B for non-critical, and 5% soft fallback checks to Model A.
[07:05] Maya (SE): Small correction — 70/30 would sum to 100; soft fallback should be a separate tiny percentage or shadow. Maybe 95/5 for critical, 80/20 for background, with shadowing for analysis.
[07:16] Jordan (AE): We're mixing up channels — let's record action: finalize the subset and the weight windows.
[07:22] [00:07:22] Daniel - MiraQ: FYI our infra prefers the weight windows to be >= 15 minutes for meaningful metrics. 1–2 minute flips are just noise.
[07:29] Maya (SE): Agreed. The gateway does incremental ramps over configurable windows. We typically recommend 15–30 minute observation windows.
[07:36] [00:08:00] Jordan (AE): Quick tangent — anyone on the call concerned about model provenance and audit logs? We know you're enterprise.
[08:05] Tom - MiraQ: Yes — audit logs are a hard requirement. We need immutable version lineage and an export we can ship to our GCP logging stack.
[08:12] Andre (Redwood CSM): That's supported. We produce per-request metadata including model hash, route policy, and decision reason. The console can ship to Cloud Logging or S3. We'll share the export spec in the security pack.
[08:25] [00:09:00] Rina - MiraQ: One more technical: when you do a rollback, do you preserve request ids so we can trace which customer requests were affected?
[09:32] Maya (SE): Yes, request ids and decision traces are preserved. We surface a timeline of routing decisions so you can query which requests saw which model.
[09:40] [00:10:00] Hannah - MiraQ: Can we get an example YAML for a version gateway rule that pins EU traffic to model C but allows fallback to B in emergencies?
[10:05] Maya (SE): I'll paste a snippet in the follow-up. It looks like: rule: match region == EU -> route weight {C:95,B:5} with fallback policy {thresholds...} — I'll send the real YAML.
[10:20] [00:11:00] Jordan (AE): Also note we saw a weird logging bug last week where model alias names escaped weirdly when used in the UI. Maya, you fixed that in the branch right?
[11:10] Maya (SE): Yep fixed — it was an encoding mismatch for some unicode characters in alias names. I added a sanitize step. Should be in the next build.
[11:20] [00:12:00] Tom - MiraQ: For the pilot success criteria — we had a doc that listed throughput, p95, cost per 1M tokens, and quality regressions threshold. Any changes?
[11:30] Jordan (AE): Let's make explicit: success = stable p95 <= 200ms for critical flows for 7 days, cost delta within budget (<+20% of current baseline), and no quality regression >3% on labeled eval set. If we hit any of these, we consider pilot failed for that variant.
[11:48] Rina - MiraQ: That lines up. Also want to include no more than 2 safety filter hits per 100k requests.
[11:55] Maya (SE): We'll surface that as a custom metric.
[12:00] [00:12:00] Jordan (AE): Any blockers on your side for locking the model subset?
[12:05] Tom - MiraQ: Need internal sign-off from product and legal on the pilot MOU. We'll aim EoW to confirm.
[12:12] Hannah - MiraQ: Also we'll need the security pack and the updated rollback YAML.
[12:18] Jordan (AE): Noted. We'll send both.
[12:22] [00:13:00] Daniel - MiraQ: One question about the fallback metrics — if we route 5% to fallback, our eval set may not cover the live distribution. Do you recommend synthetic prompts or real traffic mirroring?
[13:32] Maya (SE): Real traffic mirroring is ideal but that's heavier. For pilot, a hybrid: replay a 10k sample of recent real prompts for warmup and shadowing for a short window, plus synthetic edge cases to stress hallucination.
[13:45] [00:14:00] Jordan (AE): Ok let's talk timelines. We propose: this week finalize subset, Maya runs the 1M token A/B job and pushes CSV by Fri; next week we start gated rollout with 15m windows. agreed?
[14:05] Tom - MiraQ: Sounds right.
[14:08] [00:15:00] Jordan (AE): Any final technical clarifications?
[15:12] Rina - MiraQ: One more — for the pre-warm, how long before flip should it run? We don't want cache thrash.
[15:18] Maya (SE): Typical pre-warm runs for 10–20 minutes with your top 500 prompts. For large corp you might need longer. We'll include a pre-warm plan.
[15:26] [00:16:00] Andre (Redwood CSM): I'll also note that if you want Canary telemetry, we'll set up a temporary Grafana dashboard and a Slack alert.
[16:02] Tom - MiraQ: Good. Liam from procurement — do you have anything else?
[16:08] Liam - MiraQ: Just need the pricing delta and pilot credit note.
[16:12] Jordan (AE): We'll send that today.
[16:20] [00:17:00] Jordan (AE): Alright let's do a quick recap and next steps. Maya, can you summarize the version gateway behavior you're recommending?
[17:00] Maya (SE): Sure — recommend: immutable hash pinning with semantic alias, soft-fallback lanes at 5% for critical routes, 15–30 minute ramp windows, pre-warm before 100/0 flips, metrics: p95/p99, quality score, safety hits. Rollback: manual hard rollback for major incidents; automated soft fallback for smaller regressions.
[17:20] Jordan (AE): Tom, Rina — next steps on your side?
[17:25] Rina - MiraQ: We'll finalize model subset and confirm PII redaction scope.
[17:30] Tom - MiraQ: I'll coordinate legal and product sign-off, aim to confirm by 02/25.
[17:36] [00:18:00] Jordan (AE): I'll share the pricing delta, Maya will send YAML and run the A/B job. Andre will prepare Grafana/Slack.
[18:00] [00:18:30] Jordan (AE): Anything else?
[18:35] Hannah - MiraQ: No, thanks everyone, this was useful.
[18:40] Jordan (AE): Great — we'll follow up with the artifacts. Meeting adjourned.
[18:47] [End of recording]
